name: Bosch ME7.5.10 (VAG small petrol, 80-pin)

read_methods.notes: OBD read/write is listed for the SEAT Arosa 1.4 AKK application. Bench diagnostics use K-line. The physical boot entry point is unknown.

notes: Cost-reduced ME7.5 variant with an 80-pin connector. The ME7 checksum family applies, but OpenTune validated it on ME7.5/ME7.1 images - verify per variant. No vehicle list is given because the cited sources do not name specific applications. CAN polarity and a second ground pin are disputed between sources.

connectors.name: T80
connectors.description: 80-pin connector (Diag-Prof: T80; ecupinouts draws it as T94 of a 154-pin layout - pin numbers agree)

pins.note: Diag-Prof and ecupinouts give ground on pin 28.
Diag-Prof: CAN-High (not for diagnostics). Transpondery: CAN-L (or pin 17).
Diag-Prof: CAN-Low (not for diagnostics). Transpondery: CAN-H (or pin 18).

bench.resistor_notes: K-line only; no CAN termination needed.

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.

sources.title: Diag-Prof: VAG Bosch ME7.5.10 (pin assignment, memory)
Alientech Japan K-Suite vehicle support list (2018), SEAT Arosa 6H1 1.4 AKK with Bosch ME7.5.10

obd.protocol: K-line on T80-29. The cited sources do not identify the flash-session protocol.
obd.notes: Alientech lists OBD read/write for the 1999 and 2000 SEAT Arosa 1.4 AKK with ME7.5.10. Coverage of other hardware revisions is unknown.

bench.how: Use T80-15 for permanent +12 V, T80-27 for switched +12 V, T80-28 for ground and T80-29 for K-line diagnostics. Both pinouts agree on these numbers. Diag-Prof identifies the connector as T80 and ecupinouts labels it T94. Leave CAN pins 31 and 32 disconnected for diagnostics.

boot.notes: Alientech lists boot support for the Arosa 1.4 AKK. The cited sources identify neither an entry point nor reset timing for this board.

security.notes: The support list does not specify whether a complete diagnostic read or flash write requires security access. OpenTune ships no OEM key.
